title: Computer and Information Security
description: Threats and attackers, passwords, the CIA triad, access control and authentication, non-repudiation, encryption and hashing, email, IPsec, web, database and distributed-system security, and network auditing.

topics.title: Threats, Passwords and the CIA Triad
topics.summary: Threats to computer systems fall into malware, security breaches, denial of service, web attacks, session hijacking and DNS poisoning, carried out by hackers whose 'hats' differ in intent. Passwords, the CIA goals of confidentiality, integrity and availability, and the balance of prevention and detection are the base of any defence.
subtopics: Assessing the real level of threat
Six classes of attack: malware, breaches, DoS, web attacks, session hijacking, DNS poisoning
Hackers (white, black, grey hat), script kiddies and sneakers
Security devices and activities: firewall, proxy, IDS, authentication, auditing
Passwords: choosing, storing, verifying over a network, cracking
Confidentiality, integrity and availability; prevention and detection

topics.title: Access Control and Authentication
topics.summary: Access control decides what an authenticated subject may do to an object, through authorization, identification and authentication, access approval and accountability. The main models are discretionary, mandatory and role-based access control, and non-repudiation ties actions to a unique individual.
subtopics: Subjects and objects; capability-based and ACL-based models
Authorization, I&A, access approval and accountability
Read, write and execute permissions
DAC, MAC (sensitivity labels, rule- and lattice-based) and RBAC
Types and factors of authentication
Non-repudiation, digital signatures and trusted third parties

topics.title: Encryption and Hash Functions
topics.summary: Encryption encodes messages so only authorised parties can read them, with symmetric schemes sharing one key and asymmetric (public-key) schemes using a public and a private key. Hash functions map data of any size to a fixed-size value and support hash tables, integrity checks and digital signatures.
subtopics: Uses of encryption; symmetric and public-key encryption
Stream and block ciphers; AES, 3DES, Blowfish
Public-key infrastructure, certificate authorities and man-in-the-middle attacks
Hybrid cryptosystems; key revocation and leaked keys
Hash functions: uses and properties
Hash algorithms: perfect, universal, rolling and locality-sensitive hashing

topics.title: Email, IP, Web and Database Security
topics.summary: Email is protected by signing, body encryption and encrypted server links, but is abused by spoofing, spam worms and email bombs. IPsec secures IP traffic with AH and ESP, web applications face XSS, SQL injection and phishing, and databases and distributed systems need privileges, monitoring and their own security architecture.
subtopics: Email delivery, MIME and message authentication codes
Malicious email: spoofing, spam and worms, email bombs; tracing the source
IPsec: AH, ESP, security associations, IKE
Web attacks: cross-site scripting, SQL injection, phishing; OWASP
Database security risks, system and object privileges, evaluation
Distributed systems and the DSSA

topics.title: Network Auditing
topics.summary: Network auditing systematically examines an organisation's network infrastructure, configurations and activity for security, compliance and performance. An audit inventories assets, reviews configurations, analyses traffic, logs and user access, scans for vulnerabilities and maps compliance, following a lifecycle from planning to follow-up.
subtopics: What network auditing is and why it matters
Types of audit: security, compliance, performance, operational
Key components of a network audit
The audit lifecycle
Tools: Nmap, Wireshark, Nessus, OpenVAS and others
Log analysis, vulnerability scanning, configuration, traffic and user access auditing
